text:
Emily Chen: Heads-up — quick eval pack for customer Twine's LoRA merge (twine-lora-v2) landed on staging. Noticed a reproducible emoji normalization regression in short replies. Sharing a short sample and summary.

Raj Patel: Which merge exactly? the v2 graft or the backported token-fix? can you paste an example output vs baseline?

Emily Chen: baseline (fp16): 
```
User: Can you add a smile? 😄
Model: Sure — here's an example: I added a smile 😄
```
int4 quickpack result:
```
User: Can you add a smile? 😄
Model: Sure — here is an example: I added a smile ?
```
notice the emoji became '?' or split tokens. Ran both fp16 and our int4 pipeline — fp16 looks fine, int4 shows a ~3.8% accuracy drop on emoji-labeled tests. Command used: `./eval_quickpack --model twine-lora-v2 --quant int4 --prompts tests/emoji_small.json`

Sasha Ionescu: Hm, could be tokenizer merge + quantization interaction. Sometimes merges that touch embedding remapping or final-layer norm ordering cause strange byte-level tokenization for multibyte glyphs. Were any tokenizer merges applied in that branch? :thinking_face:

Emily Chen: The LoRA merge touched the embedding projection for new emoji variants (customer requested custom emoji mapping). We also applied a small tokenizer patch in the same PR (mapping file update).

CI Bot: CI: quick-eval for twine-lora-v2-int4 completed — status: FAIL. Delta vs baseline: 0.038 (threshold 0.02). Artifacts: s3://redwood-qev/twine/v2/int4/summary.json

Raj Patel: Possible root causes: (1) tokenizer mapping changed byte offsets, (2) quantization rounding amplified small embedding diffs, (3) final-layer norm shuffling. @Sasha can you run a quick bisect on the merge commits and run `scripts/token-map-check`?

Sasha Ionescu: Yep. I'll kick off a bisect now. Steps I'm running: 1) run token-map-check: `scripts/token-map-check --model=twine-lora-v2 --mapping=customers/twine/emoji_map.json` 2) run fp16 vs int4 diff on small reproducer with `--log-tokens` to see where splits happen. Posting logs when ready.

Emily Chen: Plan of record: 1) Sasha bisects tokenizer/merge commits and posts failing commit by EOD, 2) Raj re-runs int4 quant using per-channel asymmetric quant and compare, 3) I'll assemble a minimal reproducer prompt set and add to quickpack so future merges run it as part of preflight. If emoji drift >2% after fixes we'll roll back the merge.

Raj Patel: Re-running quant now with `quantize --model twine-lora-v2 --scheme per-channel-asym --out tmp/int4_v2_pcq` — will post results.

CI Bot: Deployed shadow fp16 variant to staging (twine-lora-v2-fp16-shadow) at 1766004360 for side-by-side smoke.

Sasha Ionescu: Initial bisect found the tokenizer_map commit 9a3f7b2 introduces a new mapping order that splits the ZWJ sequence for some emoji. Confirming reproducible failure on that commit. Will open a minimal PR to reorder mapping and run quickpack.

Emily Chen: Great — thanks all. If Sasha's mapping reorder + Raj's per-channel quant fixes don't bring drift under 2% we'll revert the LoRA merge for Twine. I added the reproducer to quickpack: tests/emoji_small.json. :thumbsup:
